To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AUC-based permutation importance measure outperforms the permutation importance measure for unbalanced data, while both permutation importance measures perform equally well for balanced data.

(i) the permutation variable importance measure (VIM) of the random forest (RF), a popular classification technique, loses its ability to rank predictors for unbalanced data, and (ii) the new area under the curve-based (AUC) permutation VIM, introduced by us in this paper, outperforms the original permutation VIM for the case of unbalance data, while both permutation VIMS have similar performance in the case of equal classes sizes.

(i) the standard permutation VMI loses its ability to distinguish between important and unimportant variables for increasing class imbalance, and (ii) our new AUC based permutation VIM is a robust alternative for unbalanced data that performs equally well as the standard permutation VIm for balanced data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of the RF-based VIMs in the case of strongly unbalance response classes.
the development of a novel permutation variable importance measure that outperforms the existing one in unbalanced settings and has equal performance in balanced settings.
the question whether the standard permutation VMI for random forests is suitable for unbalanced data and whether the AUC-based permutation importance can be a suitable alternative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the standard permutation VIF should not be used for unbalanced data, while the AUC-based permutation VI is recommended for both balanced and unbalanced data settings.
for balanced data the standard permutation VIMS and the AUC based permutation VIMs are equivalent, whereas for imbalanced data the AUC based VIMS outperforms the permutation VIMS.
for unbalanced data the standard permutation VIMS are not suitable for ranking predictors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AUC-based permutation is more robust towards class imbalances than the standard permutation VIF.
the standard permutation VIMS is outperformed for unbalanced data by our new AUV-based permutation VIM.

our AUC-based permutation importance measure outperforms the permutation importance measure based on misclassification rates for unbalanced response classes, while both VIMs have similar performance for balanced classes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new AUB-based permutation VIM is a robust and reliable VIM for unbalance data settings, while for balanced data settings the new VIM and the standard permutation VIMS perform equally well.

the performance of the variable importance measures of the random forest method depends on the class imbalance of the data and the new AUC permutation VIM is more robust to class imbalance than the standard permutation VMI.
